source.author: verg
source.text: Principio caelum ac terras camposque liquentis lucentemque globum Lunae Titaniaque astra spiritus intus alit, totamque infusa per artus mens agitat molem et magno se corpore miscet.
source.text_original: 'Principio caelum ac terras camposque liquentis / lucentemque globum Lunae Titaniaque astra / spiritus intus alit, totamque infusa per artus / mens agitat molem et magno se corpore miscet.
source.text_english: First, within the heavens, the lands, the watery plains, the shining orb of the Moon, and the Titanian stars, a spirit nourishes all things from within; poured through its limbs, mind stirs the whole mass and mingles itself with the great body.

reuse.author: hier
reuse.text: Et rursum: Coelum mihi thronus est: terra autem scabellum pedum meorum, ut intra omnia esse credendus sit: juxta illud Virgilianum: Principio coelum ac terras, camposque liquentes, Lucentemque globum lunae, Titaniaque Astra, Spiritus intus alit: totamque infusa per artus, Mens agitat molem, et magno se corpore miscet.
reuse.text_original: Et rursum: Coelum mihi thronus est: terra autem scabellum pedum meorum, ut intra omnia esse credendus sit: juxta illud Virgilianum: Principio coelum ac terras, camposque liquentes, Lucentemque globum lunae, Titaniaque Astra, Spiritus intus alit: totamque infusa per artus, Mens agitat molem, et magno se corpore miscet.
reuse.text_english: And again: Heaven is my throne, and the earth the footstool of my feet, so that he must be believed to be within all things, according to that line of Virgil: In the beginning, the heaven and the lands, and the flowing plains, and the shining orb of the moon, and the Titanian stars, the spirit within nourishes; and poured through the limbs, the mind moves the whole mass, and mingles with its great body.
